stories.title: Longpoint Buys Miami-Dade Warehouse Portfolio for $195M
stories.excerpt: Longpoint Partners has dropped $195 million on a 10-building industrial portfolio in Miami-Dade County, the Boston-based private equity firm announced. The portfolio, composed of small-bay properties, spans 729,901 square feet across 41 acres. The buildings average about 73,000 square feet with clear heights ranging from 17 to 25 feet. They’re 90 percent leased to 74 tenants, each occupying an average 10,000 square feet. “This acquisition reflects the conviction and discipline that have guided our work here: acquiring functional, well-located small-bay industrial assets with a diverse tenant base in locations where new supply is difficult to create,” Dwight Angelini, co-founder and managing partner of Longpoint, said in a statement. A representative for Longpoint has yet to provide the addresses of the properties or the name of the seller. Since 2023, Longpoint Partners has been making sizable, bulk purchases of South Florida industrial properties. It has spent nearly $600 million on 51 buildings in two portfolio acquisitions. More recently in July, the firm bought three fully leased warehouses, totaling 121,579 square feet, for $39 million. Longpoint Partners also specializes in grocery-anchored retail properties. In June, it sold a 71,191-square-foot asset near Boynton Beach to Publix for $24 million. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longpoint Partners acquires $195M, 10-building industrial portfolio in Miami-Dade, 729,901 SF.
Portfolio 90% leased to 74 tenants, small-bay properties with 17–25 ft clear heights.
Longpoint has spent ~$600M on 51 buildings in South Florida since 2023.
stories.summary: Boston-based private equity firm Longpoint Partners has acquired a 10-building, 729,901-square-foot industrial portfolio in Miami-Dade County for $195 million. The small-bay portfolio is 90% leased to 74 tenants, each averaging 10,000 square feet. Since 2023, Longpoint has deployed nearly $600 million acquiring 51 buildings in South Florida, focusing on functional, well-located assets with diverse tenant bases in supply-constrained locations.
stories.impact: Institutional capital targeting South Florida industrial reflects confidence in port-adjacent logistics demand driven by e-commerce and Latin American trade. This capital deployment and land accumulation can inflate industrial land values and construction costs, pressuring multifamily development sites competing for South Florida acreage and labor. Monitor whether logistics consolidation reduces available development land and labor pools in Miami-Dade submarkets.

stories.title: Upper Manhattan Empowerment Zone Relocates HQ to 9K SF at 119 West 125th Street
stories.excerpt: The nonprofit Upper Manhattan Empowerment Zone Development Corporation (UMEZ) is moving its nonprofit headquarters to 119 West 125th Street in Harlem, Commercial Observer has learned. UMEZ, which finances community development in Upper Manhattan, inked a 9,000-square-foot lease at the 17-story mixed-use development between Malcolm X and Adam Clayton Powell boulevards, according to Taconic Partners, a developer on the project. The nonprofit was itself a lender on the construction of the 414,000-square-foot complex, called the Urban League Empowerment Center, which officially opened its doors in late 2025. The lease term and asking rent for UMEZ’s new sixth-floor office was not disclosed, but the Class A office space likely commands a premium for the Harlem market, where office rents generally range from $30 to $55 per square foot, according to Metro Manhattan Office Space estimates. Newmark’s Chris Mongeluzo, Brian Cohen, Eric Zemachson and Chris Ventura represented ownership in the transaction, while Wharton Property Advisors CEO and President Ruth Colp-Haber represented the tenant. “UMEZ is a venerable, long-standing institution in Harlem, and I can’t think of a more appropriate building for them to take up residency,” Colp-Haber said in a statement to CO. The Urban League Empowerment Center was developed in a public-private partnership led by Empire State Development alongside Taconic Partners, L+M Development Partners, Prusik Group and BRP Companies. The block-through complex features 90,000 square feet of office space and 84,000 square feet of retail, as well as 171 affordable residences in a 17-story tower along West 126th Street. “This lease further solidifies this groundbreaking building as a leader in impactful, mission-driven development and an economic driver for the community,” said Taconic Partners’ George Tsapelas in a statement. “It is fitting for UMEZ to join the building as a tenant after years of supporting the larger development.” UMEZ’s new headqu
bullets: UMEZ nonprofit leases 9,000 SF at 119 West 125th St., Harlem mixed-use tower.
414,000-SF Urban League Empowerment Center opened late 2025; UMEZ was construction lender.
Class A Harlem office rents range $30–55/SF; premium space likely commands high end.
stories.summary: The Upper Manhattan Empowerment Zone Development Corporation (UMEZ), a community development nonprofit, leased 9,000 square feet on the sixth floor of 119 West 125th Street, a 414,000-square-foot mixed-use development in Harlem that opened in late 2025. UMEZ financed community development in Upper Manhattan and was itself a lender on the Urban League Empowerment Center's construction. Class A office rents in the Harlem market typically range from $30 to $55 per square foot.
stories.impact: UMEZ's flagship relocation to a trophy mixed-use address signals institutional confidence in Harlem's commercial and residential upside. The organization's role as both anchor tenant and construction lender on this project—and continued commitment to Upper Manhattan development financing—will likely spur additional multifamily and mixed-use investment in Central/Upper Harlem. Developers should expect rising land valuations and competitive bidding for Harlem development sites over the next 18–36 months.

stories.title: 141Willoughby Residential Conversion Snags $208M Construction Loan
stories.excerpt: Northwind Group, a Manhattan-based real estate private equity firm and debt fund manager, originated a $208-million first mortgage construction loan for 141 Willoughby St., a 24-story, 355,000-square-foot Class A tower in Downtown Brooklyn. Loan proceeds retired the existing debt on the property and will fund its partial conversion into 239 rental apartments across floors 8 through 23 and the commercial lease-up on floors 1-7, which have been rebranded as 385 Gold. The conversion is being led by a joint venture between Capstone Equities and BH3 Fund Advisors, which took control of the property in 2025 and has spent the past year in predevelopment. Originally delivered in 2023, the tower was built to full Class A institutional specification but was never occupied. The financing was arranged by Rob Turner and Ethan Pond of Eastdil Secured Savills. Northwind was represented by John Vavas of Polsinelli Group and the JV was represented by Elizabeth Smith of Goldberg Weprin Finkel Goldstein LLP. bullets: Northwind Group provides $208M construction loan for 141 Willoughby St., Downtown Brooklyn.
Capstone/BH3 converting 355,000-SF Class A tower into 239 apartments (floors 8–23) plus commercial.
Property delivered 2023 as full Class A spec but never occupied; conversion starts 2025.
stories.summary: Northwind Group originated a $208 million first mortgage construction loan for 141 Willoughby Street, a 355,000-square-foot Class A tower in Downtown Brooklyn being partially converted into 239 rental apartments by a joint venture of Capstone Equities and BH3 Fund Advisors. The property, delivered in 2023 as full institutional-spec Class A office, never leased and was repositioned to residential and retail in 2025. Loan proceeds retire existing debt and fund predevelopment and lease-up for floors 1–7 commercial space (385 Gold).
stories.impact: Office-to-residential conversion in Downtown Brooklyn signals sustained multifamily demand and lender appetite for residential conversion plays over new office development. Northwind's $208M construction financing at competitive rates reflects capital availability for repositioning; however, the 2+ year gap between delivery and conversion suggests office market weakness persists. Developers should monitor Downtown Brooklyn absorption and rental rates post-occupancy to gauge whether conversion spreads to other obsolete Class A office towers.

stories.title: Sansone Delivers Nearly 300K-SF Midlothian Logistics Facility
stories.excerpt: Sansone delivered the new Palmer Logistics facility at Midlothian Business Park. Located on 26.5 acres, the 269,700-square-foot build-to-suit logistics facility is fully leased to Palmer Logistics, a fourth-generation, Houston-based third-party logistics provider. The facility is a build-to-suit for Palmer International and will be used for the storage and distribution of hazardous materials. ARCO/Murray served as the general contractor for the project, with construction beginning in August 2025. This milestone marks the first completed development between Sansone Group and Palmer Logistics, as well as the inaugural project through the company’s programmatic funding initiative for third-party logistics (3PL) operators within the International Warehouse Logistics Association (IWLA) network. Sansone Group is a privately held, full-service commercial real estate and development firm with nearly 70 years of experience. The company hasa development footprint spanning nearly 35 states and encompassing tens of millions of square feet. The post Sansone Delivers Nearly 300K-SF Midlothian Logistics Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sansone delivers 269,700-SF Palmer Logistics build-to-suit at Midlothian Business Park, Houston.
Palmer Logistics fully leased facility for hazardous materials storage/distribution; construction Aug 2025.
First Sansone project under programmatic 3PL funding initiative with IWLA network.
stories.summary: Sansone Group delivered a new 269,700-square-foot, build-to-suit logistics facility for Palmer Logistics at Midlothian Business Park on 26.5 acres in Houston. The facility is fully leased to Palmer International for hazardous materials storage and distribution. Construction began in August 2025 and is complete; this marks Sansone's first collaboration with Palmer Logistics and the inaugural project under Sansone's programmatic funding initiative for third-party logistics operators within the International Warehouse Logistics Association network.
stories.impact: Programmatic 3PL funding signals developer-capital partnerships to accelerate supply-chain logistics build-outs in Houston and beyond. This model reduces speculative risk and enables faster lease execution. Multifamily developers competing for land in logistics-heavy markets (Houston, Dallas, Phoenix) should expect increased industrial demand, land competition, and construction labor constraints in these regions through 2027–2028. Monitor whether 3PL expansion pressures labor availability in Houston's apartment construction pipeline.

stories.title: Fengate, Mavrek Break Ground on 380-Unit Mixed-Use Residential Development in Chicago
stories.excerpt: Fengate Asset Management and Mavrek Development recently celebrated the groundbreaking of Julep West Loop, a new 25-story mixed-use residential development in Chicago’s West Loop neighborhood. The development will deliver 380 residential units, including 76 affordable units, alongside more than 21,500 square feet of commercial space, anchored by an international grocery store. Located between Fulton Market, the Chicago Loop and the Illinois Medical District, Julep West Loop will offer residents convenient access to major employment centers, transit connections and established retail, dining and entertainment amenities. Skender is serving as the general contractor and will lead construction on the project. Construction is expected to take approximately 21 months, with first occupancy anticipated in early 2028. “With demand for housing in Chicago continuing to outpace supply, now is the time to advance well-located, mixed-use communities that connect residents to jobs, transit and amenities,” said Alexander Glassman, Managing Director, U.S. Investments, Real Estate, Fengate Asset Management. bullets: Fengate/Mavrek break ground on 380-unit, 25-story mixed-use residential in Chicago West Loop.
Development includes 76 affordable units, 21,500 SF commercial anchored by international grocery.
Construction 21 months; first occupancy early 2028; located near Fulton Market, Loop, Medical District.
stories.summary: Fengate Asset Management and Mavrek Development began construction on Julep West Loop, a 25-story, 380-unit mixed-use residential development in Chicago's West Loop neighborhood. The project includes 76 affordable units and 21,500 square feet of commercial space anchored by an international grocery store. Located between Fulton Market, the Chicago Loop, and the Illinois Medical District, the project is expected to deliver in early 2028 with approximately 21 months of construction led by general contractor Skender.
stories.impact: Strong supply-constrained Chicago market supporting 380-unit delivery signals robust multifamily demand and confidence among top-tier sponsors. West Loop site selection near employment centers (Loop, Medical District) and transit validates transit-oriented development thesis. Developers should monitor Chicago absorption and rental-rate growth post-delivery; if rents remain strong, expect additional groundbreakings in West Loop and nearby North Loop submarkets in 2026–2027, potentially escalating land and labor costs.

stories.title: Evergreen Devco Moving Ahead on Denver-Area Mixed-Use Community
stories.excerpt: Evergreen Devco is building apartments, a senior living facility and retail in Thornton, just outside Denver. Creekside Gardens will span 26 acres at the southwest corner of East 104th Avenue and Washington Street. The Denver Business Journal reports the 250-unit multifamily development will sit on approximately 9.75 acres toward the center of the 26-acre site. It will include seven three-story multifamily and mixed-use buildings, along with four two-story carriage unit buildings. The apartments will feature a mix of one- and two-bedroom units. The center of the site will include a one-story clubhouse with a pool and fitness center. The apartments will include some ground-floor commercial space. Directly east of the apartments, there are 4 acres that are dedicated to an active senior living complex that is being built by Ryan Companies. The five-story building is anticipated to include 166 units. The post Evergreen Devco Moving Ahead on Denver-Area Mixed-Use Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Evergreen Devco building Creekside Gardens: 250-unit multifamily + 166-unit senior living in Thornton, CO.
26-acre site at E. 104th Ave. and Washington St.; apartments on 9.75 acres.
Senior living by Ryan Companies; mixed one/two-bedroom units, ground-floor retail, clubhouse with pool.
stories.summary: Evergreen Devco is developing Creekside Gardens, a 26-acre mixed-use community in Thornton, Colorado (southwest of Denver) comprising 250 multifamily units on 9.75 acres across seven three-story and four two-story buildings, plus a 166-unit senior living facility by Ryan Companies on 4 acres. The site includes a clubhouse, pool, fitness center, and ground-floor commercial space. Units mix one- and two-bedroom floor plans targeting both renters and active seniors.
stories.impact: Large, integrated senior + multifamily development on Denver metro periphery signals developer bet on aging-in-place demand and suburban diversification. Colorado's robust population growth and limited age-restricted supply make senior-plus-multifamily hybrids attractive. Monitor Thornton absorption and rental trends; if successful, expect similar senior-multifamily combinations in Colorado Springs, Fort Collins, and other mountain West markets, increasing land costs and construction sequencing complexity for traditional multifamily developers.

stories.title: San Antonio Agrees to Spend $60M on Spurs Arena Site
stories.excerpt: The San Antonio City Council voted to allocate $60 million toward purchasing a site for a new San Antonio Spurs arena. $115 million is needed to buy all of the land for the sports complex. The land is the former site of the Institute of Texan Cultures at Hemisfair. The deal is expected to close by the end of the year. The Spurs are planning to build a 17,000- to 18,000-seat arena in Downtown San Antonio, Texas, which will be ready in time for the 2030-31 NBA season. Mortenson and Bartlett Cocke will work together to lead construction management for the new Spurs arena, combining Mortenson’s national sports and entertainment expertise with Bartlett Cocke’s more than six decades of experience building in San Antonio and across Texas. Mortenson’s recently completed and in-progress projects include Chase Center (Golden State Warriors), Allegiant Stadium (Las Vegas Raiders), Energizer Park (St. Louis CITY SC), Climate Pledge Arena (Seattle Kraken), U.S. Bank Stadium (Minnesota Vikings), Continental Coliseum (Oklahoma City Thunder) and Athletics Ballpark (Las Vegas Athletics). The post San Antonio Agrees to Spend $60M on Spurs Arena Site appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: San Antonio allocates $60M (of $115M needed) to acquire Hemisfair Institute land for Spurs arena.
17,000–18,000-seat arena targeted for 2030–31 NBA season; land deal to close end of 2025.
Mortenson and Bartlett Cocke leading construction; Mortenson has completed Chase, Allegiant, Climate Pledge arenas.
stories.summary: San Antonio City Council voted to allocate $60 million toward a $115 million land purchase for a new San Antonio Spurs arena at the former Institute of Texan Cultures site at Hemisfair. The project targets a 17,000- to 18,000-seat arena ready for the 2030–31 NBA season, with land acquisition expected to close by year-end 2025. Mortenson and Bartlett Cocke will lead construction management, leveraging expertise in sports venues.
stories.impact: Major arena anchoring Downtown San Antonio real estate catalyst through 2030–31; public capital commitment ($60M+) signals city prioritization and likely follow-on infrastructure spending (parking, transit, streetscape). Multifamily developers should acquire land/entitlements in Downtown San Antonio and adjacent neighborhoods (Southtown, River North) immediately, as proximity to arena will drive rents and valuations 12–24 months pre-opening. Expect commercial rents to spike and construction costs to inflate in the core as arena financing and construction proceed.

stories.title: Municipal Credit Union Signs 6K-SF Lease for New Branch at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue
stories.excerpt: Municipal Credit Union (MCU) has signed a lease to open a new retail branch in Jamaica, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The not-for-profit credit union, which has locations citywide and caters only to New York City residents, signed a 15-year, roughly 6,000-square-foot lease at Michael Rosilio’s 162-15 Jamaica Avenue, according to landlord broker Augenbaum Realty. Asking rent for the ground-floor space in Jamaica’s business district was more than $100 per square foot, according to the brokerage. Josh Augenbaum and Murray Mizrachi of Augenbaum Realty represented the landlord in the transaction, while Jordan Kaplan of CBRE negotiated on behalf of the tenant. “Ownership is pleased to have provided a beautiful wide-open space on a super busy corridor where Municipal Credit Union will provide their customers with a state of the art banking experience,” Augenbaum said in a statement. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The adjacent spaces in the building were recently leased to an Olgam Life plasma donation center and a Cold Stone Creamery, which still had signage up as recently as June, Google images show. A 25,000-square-foot Fitness Factory also signed a lease in the same building at 162-11 Jamaica Avenue, also owned by the Rosilio family and brokered by Augenbaum Realty, The Real Deal reported in July. The Rosilio family purchased the property in November 2024 for $10.5 million from Ruben Azrak. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Municipal Credit Union leases 6,000 SF at 162-15 Jamaica Ave., Queens ground floor for 15 years.
Asking rent >$100/SF; Jamaica business district anchored by MCU, Olgam Life plasma center, Cold Stone.
MCU serves only NYC residents; expansion signals credit union confidence in Queens retail/population base.
stories.summary: Municipal Credit Union, a not-for-profit credit union serving only New York City residents, signed a 15-year lease for approximately 6,000 square feet at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue in Jamaica, Queens. Asking rent exceeded $100 per square foot for the ground-floor space in Jamaica's business district. Adjacent tenants include an Olgam Life plasma donation center and Cold Stone Creamery, indicating active retail leasing and neighborhood demand.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, MCU's flagship Jamaica branch expansion and $100+/SF retail rents signal rising Jamaica commercial values and institutional confidence in the neighborhood's customer base. Developers should monitor Jamaica retail rents and pedestrian traffic as indicators of residential demand uptick; if retail rents stabilize above $90/SF, multifamily site values and construction feasibility in Jamaica will strengthen significantly.

stories.title: Multifamily Developer LCOR Buys Taconic’s UES Life Sciences Site for $73M
stories.excerpt: Taconic Partners has parted with another life sciences project in Manhattan. The developer sold 309 East 94th Street on the Upper East Side for $73 million, according to city records filed Thursday. The buyer, LCOR, develops multifamily properties along the East Coast and recently entered South Florida’s residential market. The sale of the 87,000-square-foot assemblage between First and Second avenues marks a slight premium on the $70 million all-cash deal that last transferred the site from the Karten family to Taconic and its joint venture partners in December 2021. The joint venture, composed of Taconic subsidiary Elevate Research Properties, Nuveen Real Estate and Flatiron Equities, planned to construct a 200,000-square-foot, Class A research lab. The eight-story Iron Horse Labs was designed to benefit from proximity to major academic medical institutions Rockefeller University, Mount Sinai Medical Center and NYC Health + Hospitals. The project secured a $79 million construction loan from Ares Commercial Real Estate in 2022 and began construction in 2023, but its current progress is uncertain. The site still contains a five-story loft-style building, a two-story garage and an auto shop, according to The Real Deal. The Upper East Side deal follows Taconic’s $188 million sale of West End Labs at 125 West End Avenue in July. That asset, part of Taconic’s 3.4-acre West End Campus, was acquired by Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square Foundation. The life sciences sector continues to navigate post-pandemic vacancies. Leasing volume for New York City’s life sciences sector fell 84 percent in the first three months of 2026 compared to the previous quarter, according to CBRE data. It’s unclear who brokered the sale at 309 East 94th Street. Spokespeople for Taconic and LCOR did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: LCOR purchases Taconic's Upper East Side life sciences site (309 E. 94th St.) for $73M.
87,000-SF assemblage; Taconic's planned 200,000-SF Class A research lab (Iron Horse Labs) abandoned.
LCOR, multifamily developer, repositioning for residential; $79M Ares construction loan remains outstanding.
stories.summary: Multifamily developer LCOR has acquired 309 East 94th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side for $73 million, a slight premium on Taconic Partners' $70 million purchase in December 2021. The 87,000-square-foot assemblage was originally planned as Iron Horse Labs, a 200,000-square-foot Class A research facility designed to capitalize on proximity to Rockefeller University, Mount Sinai, and NYC Health + Hospitals. Taconic's original joint venture partners included Elevate Research Properties, Nuveen Real Estate, and Flatiron Equities; a $79 million Ares construction loan was issued in 2022 but the project was shelved.
stories.impact: Flight from speculative life sciences development to residential repositioning signals weakening demand for trophy research lab space and capital redeployment toward housing. The $79M Ares construction loan likely remains on Taconic's balance sheet; LCOR's conversion to multifamily will require new financing and may trigger loan restructuring. Monitor other stalled Manhattan life sciences projects (Kendall Square, Hudson Yards) for similar pivots. Multifamily developers should view Manhattan's Upper East Side life sciences assemblages as acquisition opportunities; proximity to major medical anchors and transit will support residential absorption and premium rents.

stories.title: CRE Finance Council Names Paul Vanderslice New CEO
stories.excerpt: The CRE Finance Council has turned to a commercial real estate banking veteran as its next leader. The leading trade organization for commercial real estate finance professionals announced Friday morning that Paul Vanderslice, who has led BMO’s commercial mortgage-backed securities platform for the last six years, will be assuming the role of president and CEO effective Sept. 30. He will replace Lisa Pendergast, who retired in August after 10 years leading CREFC. Vanderslice’s new role leading CREFC will also mean his departure from BMO with his last day there scheduled for Sept. 29. Prior to joining BMO Capital Markets in 2020, Vanderslice held senior leadership roles in CRE finance at CCRE and Citigroup. He has been a CREFC member for nearly three decades, including a stint as chair of both the group’s executive committee and board of governors from 2012 to 2013. “Paul brings deep industry expertise, a longstanding commitment to CREFC, and a clear understanding of the issues and opportunities facing our members,” Toby Cobb, co-founder and co-managing partner of 3650 Capital and chair of CREFC’s executive committee and board of governors, said in a statement. “Having previously served as chair and as a current member of the board of governors, Paul knows the organization and the industry exceptionally well. We look forward to his leadership as we enter this next chapter.” Vanderslice joined BMO Capital Markets, a subsidiary of Bank of Montreal, in September 2020 to launch and lead the bank’s CMBS platform after spending two years as CEO of CCRE. He spent more than 30 years at Citigroup, where he helped build up the bank’s CMBS business. Leland Bunch, chair of CREFC’s CEO search committee and managing director at Bank of America, said a number of candidates were considered from across the CRE industry and leasing U.S. trade associations. “Paul distinguished himself through his lifelong commitment to commercial real estate and his longstanding dedication to CREFC,” B
bullets: Paul Vanderslice (BMO CMBS, 6 years) named CRE Finance Council CEO effective Sept. 30, 2025.
Vanderslice succeeds Lisa Pendergast (10 years); brings CREFC board/exec committee experience since 1990s.
Prior roles at CCRE, Citigroup; BMO departure effective Sept. 29; industry leadership focus.
stories.summary: The CRE Finance Council announced Paul Vanderslice as its new president and CEO, effective September 30, 2025, succeeding Lisa Pendergast who retired in August after 10 years. Vanderslice spent six years leading BMO's commercial mortgage-backed securities platform and held prior senior CRE finance roles at CCRE and Citigroup. He has been a CREFC member for nearly three decades and previously chaired both the executive committee and board of governors (2012–2013).
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, Vanderslice's CMBS expertise and industry connectivity signal CREFC's continued focus on CRE capital markets and debt structures. Multifamily developers relying on CMBS, bond issuance, or institutional debt should expect stable industry advocacy and potential evolution in financing standards as Vanderslice brings BMO's securitization best practices and risk frameworks to trade-group leadership.
